speed_hint_fast: High concurrency, short timeout, quickest, may miss slow responses.
speed_hint_normal: Balanced default, good for most targets.
speed_hint_cautious: Low concurrency, longer timeout, gentler on the target.
empty_description: Enter a target above and click Start scan.
guide_intro: A gobuster-style content discovery scan: brute-forces common directory and file names against a target to find pages that exist but aren't linked from anywhere.
guide_step1_body: Requests <0>{{example}}</0> for each entry in SecLists' <1>{{file}}</1>. "Top 100/1000" are quick passes; "full" is the most thorough but slowest and noisiest against the target.
guide_step2_body: Appends each extension to every word too: e.g. entering <0>{{ex1}}</0> also tries <1>{{ex2}}</1> and <2>{{ex3}}</2> alongside the bare <3>{{ex4}}</3>. Useful for catching forgotten backup files or a specific server-side language.
guide_step3_body: <0>Fast</0> sends many requests at once with a short timeout; <1>Cautious</1> spaces it out, easier on a target that rate-limits or has a WAF. <2>Normal</2> is a balanced default.
guide_step4_title: Click "Start scan" and watch it stream in
guide_step4_body: Every candidate is requested (redirects are reported, not followed; a 301 is itself a finding). Results appear in the table live. "Stop" cancels a running scan at any point.
guide_step5_body: 404s are hidden by default since most of a large wordlist won't exist; toggle "Show 404s" to see every attempt. Watch for <0>401</0>/<1>403</1> (something's there but protected) and <2>3xx</2> redirects, not just <3>200</3>.
guide_footer_note: This sends real HTTP requests to the target: a full wordlist run can be thousands of requests. Only run this against hosts you're authorized to test.
